title: Money the government borrowed from the Central Bank
summary: 'Ways & Means' is an overdraft the Central Bank can give the Federal Government to cover short-term cash gaps. By December 2022 the balance had reached ₦22.7 trillion, far above the legal limit. In 2023 it was converted into long-term bonds, so it is now public debt. What the money paid for has not been itemised publicly, and the advances have been investigated.
simple: The government borrowed ₦22.7 trillion from the Central Bank as an overdraft, far above the legal limit. In 2023 it was turned into long-term debt that Nigerians will be paying for decades. No public breakdown shows what the money paid for.

verdict.text: What it paid for: no public record found
Investigated by a presidential investigator and the Senate
Now a 40-year debt at 9% interest. Repayment began in 2026

gaps: We could not find a public, itemised account of what the ₦22.7 trillion paid for.
The findings of the Senate's 2024 ad hoc committee are not yet reflected here.

timeline.text: Ways & Means advances to the Federal Government reach ₦22.7 trillion.
The Senate approves turning the ₦22.7 trillion into a 40-year loan at 9% interest, with no repayment of the principal for 3 years.
A presidential special investigator's report alleges that the advances breached Section 38 of the CBN Act. These are allegations, not court findings.
The Senate approves converting a further ₦7.3 trillion outstanding balance.
The Senate sets up a 17-member ad hoc committee to probe a reported ₦30 trillion in Ways & Means advances. That figure is disputed.
The 3-year pause ends and repayment of the principal begins. The balance falls to about ₦22.1 trillion.

nodes.label: Central Bank of Nigeria (overdraft)
nodes.simple: The Central Bank lent the government money like a bank overdraft, far above the legal limit of 5% of revenue.
nodes.description: Section 38 of the CBN Act 2007 limits Ways & Means advances to 5% of the previous year's federal revenue and requires repayment by the end of the year. By 19 December 2022 the balance stood at ₦22.7 trillion.

evidence.title: Securitisation of the N22.7trn Ways and Means

nodes.label: Federal Government of Nigeria
nodes.simple: The government spent it outside the approved budget. In 2023 it became long-term debt.
nodes.description: The money was spent outside the approved budget. In May 2023 the National Assembly approved turning it into a 40-year loan at 9% interest, with a 3-year pause on repaying the principal. The previous rate had been about 21%. Repayment began in 2026.
